Vanilla builds scopes like `GuiScope.SetRoot( GetPlayer.MakeScope ).AddScope( 'second', GetTenetType('tenet_aniconism').MakeScope )` and hands them to a custom text; that text's file notes that `scope:second` is the tenet, so script can reach the object under that name.

label: Custom text
summary: The text a custom localization (a scripted text that picks its wording by conditions) produces for this scope.
details: It takes one value: the custom localization's key in quotes. Vanilla writes `SCOPE.Custom('BG_GameType')` in board game events to name the game being played; BG_GameType is made for characters, so the scope's object is used to pick the text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

label: Finish scope
summary: Finishes a scope built with SetRoot and AddScope, and hands it back for use.
details: Vanilla ends chains such as `GuiScope.SetRoot( Character.MakeScope ).End` with it before passing the scope to a scripted GUI, to run it (`ScriptedGui.Execute`) or to check whether it shows (`IsShown`).

label: Saved flag
summary: The flag saved under the given name in this scope, as text.
details: It takes one value: the name the flag was saved under. Vanilla's artifact texts write `SCOPE.GetFlagName('fastener_metal')` and pass the result to a custom text that turns the flag into words, such as the metal of a brooch.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name the flag is saved under.
fields.values: a name in quotes, such as 'fastener_metal'

label: Root
summary: The root object of this scope (what the text or script is about).
details: Vanilla reads it as a character, as in `SCOPE.GetRootScope.Char.GetFaith.GetAdjective` or `SCOPE.GetRootScope.GetCharacter.GetCulture.GetNameNoTooltip` in decision and event tooltips. The game documents no return type.

label: Script value breakdown
summary: The breakdown of how the named script value is worked out for this scope, for the interface to show.
details: It takes one value: the script value's key. Vanilla's cardinals window builds a scope with a character as root and uses the breakdown of values such as 'pam_papal_pious_priority_value' as the data of a part of the window. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the script value.
fields.values: a script value key in quotes

label: Script value description
summary: Going by its name, a text describing how a named script value is worked out for the top scope.
details: It returns text. Vanilla never uses it on this type; uses on other types in the tournament tooltips are only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by similar uses, the script value key.
fields.values: a script value key in quotes

label: Saved number
summary: A number that was saved under the given name and is printed in a text.
details: Vanilla script saves such numbers with `save_scope_value_as` and its texts print them with TopScope.GetValue('name'), for example the herd given at a coronation, a payment owed in an event or the glory an accolade loses. The name must match the one used when saving.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name the number was saved under.

label: Script value
summary: The result of the named script value, worked out for this scope, as a number.
details: It takes one value: the script value's key. Vanilla uses it very often in texts, for example `EmptyScope.ScriptValue('feast_activity_cost_discount_min_value')` shown as a percentage in a building description.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the script value.
fields.values: a script value key in quotes

label: Top scope itself
summary: Going by its name, the top scope itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it as an argument in the rite creation window: DoctrineItem.ShouldDisplay( TopScope.Self ) and DoctrineItem.CanPick( TopScope.Self ). Going by those names, they decide whether a doctrine is shown and can be picked. The game documents no return type.

label: Set root
summary: Sets the root object (what the script is about) of a scope being built, and hands the scope back so more can be chained.
details: It takes one value: the object. Vanilla starts chains with `GuiScope.SetRoot( GetPlayer.MakeScope )` or `GuiScope.SetRoot( Character.MakeScope )`, adds more with AddScope, and passes the scope to a custom text or a scripted GUI.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The object to use as root.
fields.values: an object made into a scope with MakeScope

label: Saved army
summary: Going by its name, an army saved in the top scope under the given name.
details: The "s" prefix and the argument are not explained by the game; that it reads a saved army rests on the name alone. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by the name, the saved name.

label: Saved character (short)
summary: The character saved under the given name in this scope.
details: It takes one value: the saved scope's name. Vanilla uses it very often to hand a saved character to a character custom text, as in `ROOT.Char.Custom2('RelationToMeShort', SCOPE.sC('generous_courtier'))`, which names how that character is related to the root. It is a short form of sCharacter. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name the character is saved under.
fields.values: a saved scope name in quotes, such as 'adventure_target'

label: Saved casus belli
summary: Going by its name, a casus belli (a war's justification) saved in the top scope under the given name.
details: That CB means casus belli rests on the name alone. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by the name, the saved name.

label: Saved character
summary: The character saved under the given name in this scope.
details: It takes one value: the saved scope's name. Vanilla's house feud texts write `SCOPE.sCharacter('house_feud_rival').GetHouse.GetBaseName` to name the rival's house. sC is a short form. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name the character is saved under.
fields.values: a saved scope name in quotes, such as 'house_feud_rival'

label: Access tradition group
summary: A function on a group of cultural traditions that, going by its name, hands back the group itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Tradition category
summary: The category of a group of cultural traditions, which the add tradition window uses to tell its tabs apart.
details: Vanilla uses it in the add tradition window: clicking a category tab passes it to AddTraditionWindow.SetTraditionCategory, and AddTraditionWindow.HasTraditionCategory with it decides whether the tab shows as pressed and whether its list is visible. The game documents no return type.

label: Tradition group name
summary: The display name of a group of cultural traditions.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of each category tab in the add tradition window, and in the culture divergence window followed by the number of possible traditions of the group in brackets.
